editorial:
You follow Lou, a teenage tomboy in a small California town who looks up to her single dad. One night he has a date over and sends her out, and that push out the door becomes the start of something bigger. The film has a quiet, sun-baked feel that pulls you into her world and makes you care about what happens next.

The acting feels natural and grounded, and the pacing lets you sit with Lou's emotions without rushing. It is slow at times, and the story stays small, so if you want big action this may not be for you. But if you enjoy gentle coming-of-age stories, you will find a lot to like. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Lou wanders to the edge of town and spends the night among strangers and new friends who show her a different way to live. She realizes her identity is hers to shape, not just a copy of her dad. When she returns home, she is calmer and more sure of herself, and her dad sees her differently too. The twist is that being pushed out was the thing that helped her grow up.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves gentle coming-of-age stories and small-town character dramas.
